Both clocks were synthetic. Here is what happens when the model uses the real one.

The pipeline detects real beats with Beat This!, then throws them away: it fits one constant tempo and one phase and rebuilds a metronome, bt = arange(phase, duration, period). Every chord boundary it prints is a time read off that metronome — 0.2 ms from the lattice, 60–190 ms from the beats it actually heard. This page is the listen test.

Read the pictures like this

The grey curve is spectral-flux onset strength — a chord-model-free measure of "something was struck here". Blue solid lines are the beats Beat This! detected. Red dashed lines are the shipped lattice. Where blue sits on the bumps and red sits between them, the lattice is describing a performance that is not happening.

Sampled at each grid and divided by the curve's own mean (1.00 = chance): detected beats score 1.33–3.44x on all seven benchmark songs and beat a 200-draw random-phase null at p<0.005 on six of them; the lattice scores 0.83–1.16x and sits inside the null on the same six. The seventh, Every Breath You Take, is machine-steady — there the two grids are the same grid, and that song is included below as the control.

Does it pay? The honest 2x2

The trap: the benchmark's reference is also a metronomic lattice, so moving only one side breaks an agreement between two wrong clocks. All four cells, pooled duration-weighted over the 7 frozen songs, family-level partial_credit:

model gridreference as-isreference retimed
synthetic lattice (shipped)0.66790.6619
snapped to detected beats0.66440.6719
decoded on detected beats0.66470.6722

The diagonal is the whole story: each clock scores best against the reference on the same clock. Both-synthetic 0.6679 → both-real 0.6722 is +0.43 pp. Small. The off-diagonal cells lose 0.3–0.6 pp, which is exactly the −0.58 pp that retiming the reference alone cost last time.

The sharper test: the boundary collar

Blank a ±0.25 s collar around every reference boundary and rescore. Whatever that buys is error concentrated at the boundaries. If the lattice was the cause, the collar's payoff must shrink once both sides are on real beats — and it cannot be faked by two clocks agreeing.

songshipped
(latt./as-is)		real beats
(det./retimed)		Δppcollar gain
shipped		collar gain
real beats
bein_green0.65550.6645+0.90+1.45+0.62
blue_bossa (guard refused)0.57080.5708+0.00+6.13+6.13
blue_bossa_backing0.77930.7917+1.24+5.89+2.95
close_to_you0.74650.7536+0.71+3.03+2.08
every_breath_you_take (control: no drift)0.73480.7235-1.13+4.28+3.04
georgia_on_my_mind0.51740.5498+3.24+4.01+1.02
stand_by_me (Occam re-lattices)0.73050.7180-1.25+2.25+3.53
POOLED0.6679 0.6722 +0.43 +4.97 +3.75

Pooled, the collar's payoff falls from +4.97 pp to +3.75 pp. Restricted to the five songs where the real grid actually reached the output (Blue Bossa is refused by the coverage guard; Stand By Me's chords are re-laid onto a second lattice by the Occam post-pass), it falls from +4.04 to +2.13 pp — and on strict equality from +1.62 to +0.31 pp. Roughly half of the boundary-localised error was the wrong clock. The other half is not.

What this does not fix

  • Blue Bossa — 25.2% of its beats are never detected. The guard refuses the re-lay rather than interpolating into the holes; its score is unchanged to four decimals. Nothing here helps a song the beat tracker fails on.
  • The Occam post-pass rebuilds its own lattice. It re-lays the chord spans onto arange(phi*beat, ..., bar_period), so on any song where it fires (Stand By Me here) the real-beat grid is silently undone downstream. Second site, not fixed.
  • The remaining ~half of the collar gain. After both clocks are real, the ±0.25 s collar still buys +2.13 pp. That residue is not a timing defect — it is wrong labels near real changes, plus reference labels Louis has already flagged as wrong on 12% of the benchmark.
  • Every Breath You Take loses 1.13 pp root. Its lattice was already correct; moving the reference under a model that did not need moving costs it.

Default is OFF. HARMONIA_REAL_BEAT_GRID=snap re-lays the emitted boundary times; =grid decodes on the detected beats outright. Unset, both entry points return their input object unchanged (proved end-to-end: identical chords on 3 songs vs the code with the brick removed). Built gridunify_page.py; audio embedded as data: URIs (0.7 MB total).
